framing.definition: OOD is evaluated along condition shift (C), fault-semantic shift (F), and combined C+F axes; each run declares which support boundary it tests.
framing.dataset_limit: The public training set is 26 WLTP recordings with 2-7 recordings per known fault family. It is not sufficient to claim broad cross-cycle, cross-engine or high-coverage fault-specific generalization without additional independent data.
framing.unknown_slot: f_x is a model output slot for a fault not assigned to one of the four named classes; the presence of the slot does not prove the public data contain genuinely novel fault mechanisms.

axes.question: Does the detector retain known-fault recognition when the operating cycle is absent from fitting and calibration?
axes.training_support: All fitted and calibrated examples come from declared training cycles only.
axes.test_support: Entire held-out driving cycles, with all recordings and temporal windows kept together.
axes.label_policy: Known fault labels remain known; unsupported cycles may be not_evaluated if regime support and calibration do not cover them.
required_controls: same fault family and severity support where available
axes.qualification: Do not call a random row split a C-shift experiment.

axes.question: Are changes in ambient pressure/temperature incorrectly treated as faults when they arise from lab/environment differences?
axes.training_support: Declare fitted ambient pressure/temperature envelope from training recordings only.
axes.test_support: Hold out complete recordings in predeclared ambient strata outside or near the training envelope.
axes.label_policy: Ambient variables are disturbance context; ambient movement alone must not be relabelled as a fault.
required_controls: do not split rows from same recording
report overlap between ambient and fault conditions
axes.qualification: If ambient strata are confounded with fault labels or drive cycle, report non-identifiability rather than a clean causal result.

axes.question: Can the system refrain from assigning an untrained fault family to a known class?
axes.training_support: Exclude every recording of one fault family from fitting, feature selection, calibration and model selection.
axes.test_support: Evaluate the excluded family as unknown (f_x) on independent recordings, with no-fault and known-fault controls.
axes.label_policy: For the strict open-set track, the held-out family maps to unknown at inference even though the evaluator retains its hidden family identity for analysis.
required_controls: held-out family absent from all model-selection stages
no hidden family identity in model inputs
recording-level split and source-bound label mapping
axes.data_status: surrogate_only_on_known_families; genuinely novel physical fault data not established
axes.qualification: This leave-one-known-family-out proxy tests label-space exclusion, but is not equivalent to discovering an entirely new physical mechanism.

axes.question: Does an unseen fault family remain safely unknown under an unseen operating cycle?
axes.training_support: Training and calibration include neither the held-out fault family nor the held-out driving cycle.
axes.test_support: Independent recordings from the joint held-out fault-family × held-out-cycle cell.
axes.label_policy: Held-out fault family remains unknown; unseen cycle remains a separate support flag.
required_controls: no tuning on either held-out axis
axes.qualification: Do not infer combined-shift robustness from separate C-only and F-only experiments.

axes.question: Does a known fault remain detectable at magnitudes not represented during fitting?
axes.training_support: Fit on declared magnitude ranges for each fault family.
axes.test_support: Hold out complete recordings from predeclared magnitude bands.
axes.label_policy: Fault family remains known; severity estimate is evaluated separately from detection/isolation.
required_controls: magnitude derived from source filename or injection log and audited
axes.qualification: A within-family severity shift is not a novel fault-semantic shift.

axes.question: Does sensor drift, bias, dropout or calibration change induce false faults or hide real faults?
axes.training_support: Declare sensor calibration, noise and availability envelope.
axes.test_support: Use independent recordings with documented sensor-chain changes; synthetic corruption is reported as a separate controlled stress test.
axes.label_policy: Separate sensor fault from sensor-chain uncertainty and plant fault; preserve ambiguous alternatives.
required_controls: channel dictionary and physical signal roles frozen
injected corruption magnitude/seed bound in manifest
axes.qualification: Synthetic corruption is not evidence of sensor or plant robustness in service.

cross_engine_and_fleet.rule: Requires independent engine identities or fleet units in both development and held-out evaluation; repeated recordings from one engine do not substitute for independent engines.

statistical_gates.underpowered_rule: Below minimum or with confounded support, report descriptive results and intervals only; do not qualify the stratum.
statistical_gates.uncertainty: Cluster by recording/engine run; never bootstrap 20 Hz sample rows as if independent.

hard_gates: declare shift axes before model fitting and confirmatory testing
keep whole recordings, overlapping windows and their event labels within a single split
prevent held-out cycles/fault families from model fitting, feature selection, calibration and threshold selection
report known-class retention separately from unknown-fault detection and abstention
joint C+F robustness needs direct joint-cell test data
unsupported support regions are not normal by default
condition covariates such as ambient pressure and temperature are not fault labels
cross-engine and fleet claims require independent engine/fleet identities
report independent-unit counts and uncertainty for every claimed stratum
